bilingual.notes: Florida has no separate bilingual education certification or endorsement. Bilingual program delivery is staffed by ESOL-credentialed teachers, often paired with a World Language certification (e.g., Spanish K-12) where appropriate.

eld.notes: Florida offers two ESOL credentials: (1) the standalone ESOL K-12 certification under Rule 6A-4.0245 (FTCE 047 ESOL K-12 subject area exam, or major in ESOL); and (2) the ESOL academic endorsement under Rule 6A-4.0244, which requires 15 semester hours across five areas (Methods, Curriculum and Materials, Cross-Cultural Communication, Applied Linguistics, Testing and Evaluation) — or a Florida district's approved inservice add-on program. The State Board adopted new ESOL endorsement standards on 2025-08-20 under Rule 6A-4.02451 (effective Sep 2025); approved programs must submit revised matrices to FLDOE by 2026-06-01. No language-proficiency exam (LOTE) is required.

sei.notes: Florida operates under the LULAC v. State Board of Education Consent Decree (1990-08-14), which mandates ESOL training scaled by teacher category: Category I (Language Arts/English/Reading/Elementary/ESE serving ELLs) needs the full ESOL endorsement (15 SH or 300 inservice points) or FTCE 047 plus 2 ESOL courses; Category II (math/science/social studies/computer literacy) needs 1 course or 60 inservice points; Category III (fine arts/electives, SLPs, OT/PT) needs 1 course or 18 inservice points; Category IV (school-based administrators and counselors) needs 1 course. Training is conditional on serving ELLs in covered roles, so this is not equivalent to the AZ/CA/MA model where SEI is mandated for all teachers regardless of student population.

history.title: LULAC v. State Board of Education Consent Decree entered
history.description: The federal consent decree settling LULAC v. SBE established Florida's framework for serving ELs and trained teachers, including the category-conditional ESOL training requirements (Categories I–IV) that remain the operative SEI-style mandate in Florida. The decree is the foundation for Rules 6A-4.0244 (endorsement) and 6A-4.0245 (standalone K-12 certification).

history.title: Florida adopts the State Seal of Biliteracy
history.description: Florida Statute § 1003.432 (HB 7029, 2016) authorizes a Gold and Silver Seal of Biliteracy on the high-school diploma for graduates demonstrating proficiency in English plus one or more world languages.

history.title: State Board adopts 2025 Florida Teacher Standards for ESOL Endorsement
history.description: The State Board adopted Rule 6A-4.02451 establishing new ESOL endorsement standards (effective September 2025), replacing the 2010 standards. The five-strand structure (Culture, Applied Linguistics, Methods of Teaching, Curriculum and Materials, Testing and Evaluation) is preserved; approved programs must submit revised matrices to FLDOE by 2026-06-01.
